chunks: Al-Hasan ibn 'Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to me from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: Any believer whose eyes shed a tear for the killing of Al-Husayn ibn 'Ali, until it runs down his cheek, Allah will provide for him thereby rooms in Paradise where he will dwell for long ages.

And any believer whose eyes shed a tear until it runs down his cheek for us, due to the affliction that touched us from our enemy in this world, Allah will provide for him thereby a good settlement in Paradise.

And any believer who is touched by affliction for us, and his eyes shed a tear until it runs down his cheek from the pain of what was endured for us, Allah will turn away affliction from his face and make him safe on the Day of Resurrection from His Wrath and from the Fire.

key_terms.مُبَوَّأَ صِدْقٍ: A good settlement / abode of truth

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for crying over the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the profound spiritual efficacy of emotional connection (*mawadda*) to the Ahl al-Bayt, a core tenet in Shia theology. It distinguishes between tears shed specifically for Imam Husayn’s martyrdom, which grant multi-layered Paradise, and those for the general afflictions of the Imams, which ensure divine protection and deliverance from Hellfire. This underscores the Shia belief that grief for the Imams is not merely sentimental but a transformative act of worship that expiates sins and secures eternal bliss.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā narrated to me from his father, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ‘Alā ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Ja’far (Imam Bāqir (a.s.)), who said: ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain (Imam Sajjād (a.s.)) used to say: Any believer who cries over Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.) with (even) one tear running down his cheek will be rewarded by Allāh for that tear; he will be made to dwell in rooms in Paradise where he will stay for long ages.

Any believer, who cries over us with (even) one tear running down his cheek because of his grief over the way in which our enemies hurt us in this life, will be rewarded by Allāh for that tear; he will be made to dwell in good settlements in Paradise.

And any believer, who cries with (even) one tear running down his cheek because of his suffering from the pain of being hurt in our way, will be kept away from the afflictions of the Day of Judgment by Allāh and he will be safe from Allāh’s Wrath and from Hell. The above Ḥadīth has also been narrated to me through the following chain: My father, and all of my scholars, from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ḥamzah ibn ‘Ali Al-Ash’ari, from Ḥasan ibn Mu’āwiyah ibn Wahab, from someone who narrated to him, from Abī Ja’far (a.s.).
